title: Milan (5.13)
hookLine: Augustine arrives as professor and meets Ambrose
tomorrow: what was the bishop doing that Augustine couldn't stop watching?

lines: THE FIRST PERSON WHO SAYS YOUR NAME.
cards: A new job in a new city, and the first person who learns your name and says it right.

Augustine gets a post in Milan, teaching rhetoric, the art of public speaking; the city's prefect tries him with a set speech, likes it, and sends him north. And who is waiting at the end of the road?

teach.h: TO MILAN I CAME, TO AMBROSE.
teach.b: Augustine tells it in one breath: to Milan I came, to Ambrose the bishop.
Then: that man of God received me like a father, and welcomed my coming as a bishop should. Notice what Augustine wasn't doing. He wasn't searching for faith.
He began to love Ambrose, he says, at first not as a teacher of truth, which he'd given up hoping to find in the Church, but as a man who was kind to him.
He went to hear Ambrose preach, and he's honest about why: to test whether the well-known eloquence lived up to its name.
He hung on the style and cared nothing for the content. Then something slipped past his guard.

teach.h: THE TRUTH CAME IN WITH IT.
teach.b: Along with the words he enjoyed came the meaning he didn't plan to take in. He couldn't keep them apart.
As he opened his heart to how well Ambrose spoke, how truly he spoke came in too, little by little. Yesterday, a charming speaker with little underneath.
Today, a fine speaker with a great deal underneath, and before either, a welcome, the way a father receives a son at the door.

how: Catholics honor Ambrose as a saint and Doctor of the Church. Parishes and bishops still take welcome seriously: receiving newcomers, inquirers and people returning, often before any talk of belief.

o: the city where Augustine was born and raised
the city where Augustine studied with Cicero
the city where a bishop welcomed Augustine

games.q: the road to Milan — tap the pairs.

s: Augustine went to Milan looking for God
he went for a job. the welcome found him first.
at first Augustine loved Ambrose as a kind man, not a teacher of truth
he'd given up hoping to find truth in the Church.
Augustine listened to the sermons for their message from the start
he came to judge the eloquence; the meaning slipped in with the words.

games.q: a new family moves in next door, not your faith, and you're not sure what to say about religion. what does Milan suggest comes first?
o: the welcome: their names, their boxes, a plate of food.
a clear talk about what you believe, so it's honest.
keeping your distance until you know where they stand.
games.why: Ambrose received Augustine like a father before any argument. the truth came in later, with the words Augustine came to judge.

practice: Stand, if you can, and turn to face the door of the room you're in. Let your shoulders drop and your hands hang open, the posture of someone ready to greet whoever comes through.
Hold it while you remember one person who once received you kindly, before you'd proved anything, and give thanks for them, to God or to the quiet.

wordCard.voice: Milan. The city where Augustine came to teach rhetoric, and where a bishop named Ambrose received him like a father.

orig.note: Latin, Confessions 5.13: he received me like a father.

carryVoice: Your line: the bishop received me, and the welcome came before the argument. Day done.
